title: SAMARTH SCHEME
body_text:
Under Samarth Scheme fund is allocated directly to the implementing partners, there is no allocation of fund State & District wise under the scheme. The year-wise details of fund allocated, released and spent under the Samarth Scheme from the year 2017 to March 2026 as are given below:
(Rs. in crore)
S. No. Financial Year Allocated (RE) Total funds released (AE) 1 2017-18 100 100.00 2 2018-19 42 16.99 3 2019-20 102.10 72.06 4 2020-21 80 90.70 5 2021-22 90 85.69 6 2022-23 25 23.27 7 2023-24 115 114.99 8 2024-25 331.00 260.26 9 2025-26 260.00 255.42
Samarth (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textiles Sector) of Ministry of Textiles provides demand driven, placement-oriented skilling programmes in the organized textile and related sectors, covering the entire value chain of textiles, excluding Spinning and Weaving on pan India basis. Under the Samarth scheme, a total of 6.17 lakh beneficiaries have successfully trained (certified), of which 5.17 lakh beneficiaries have been provided placement since the inception of the Scheme up to March 2026.
Under the Samarth Scheme, a total of 27,497 beneficiaries have been placed in the State of Rajasthan, including the Jhunjhunu LokSabha Constituency, since the inception up to March 2026. Out of these, 23,102 beneficiaries are women, 10,727 belong to the Scheduled Castes (SC) category, and 4,753 belong to the Scheduled Tribes (ST) category.
A total of 370 Implementing Partners (IPs) have been empanelled under the Samarth Scheme from the year 2017 till date. The details of the empanelled Implementing Partners are given below:
S. No. Type of Implementation Partner Number ofImplementation Partner 1 Textile Industry/ Industry Associations 327 2 State/ Central Government Agencies 38 3 Sectoral Organizations 5
Under the Samarth Scheme, training targets are allocated directly to the Implementing Partners (IPs). An IP may establish and operate training centres across various States and districts across the country based on its approved project. Therefore, no state-wise or district-wise training targets are allocated under the scheme. Further, based on the performance and progress of implementation, the training targets of 97 Implementing Partners have been rationalized, while the training targets of 32 Implementing Partners have been cancelled due to slow progress or non-commencement of training activities.
This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today.
****
MAM/VN
(Lok Sabha US Q3791)

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Textiles provided data on the Samarth Scheme, a skill development programme for the textile sector. Since its inception in 2017 up to March 2026, the scheme has trained and certified 6.17 lakh beneficiaries, of whom 5.17 lakh secured placement, through 370 empanelled Implementing Partners. Funds are allocated directly to Implementing Partners rather than state/district-wise, with cumulative releases fluctuating yearly, and Rajasthan alone recorded 27,497 placements including significant representation of women, SC and ST beneficiaries.
enrichment.context:
Samarth (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textiles Sector) is a central sector skilling scheme launched in 2017 under the Ministry of Textiles to address the shortage of skilled manpower in the organized textile sector, which is one of India's largest employment generators after agriculture. It covers the entire textile value chain except spinning and weaving, which are addressed through other skill missions, and is implemented in a demand-driven, placement-linked mode through industry bodies, government agencies, and sectoral organizations rather than through direct state-wise allocations. This model reflects the broader shift in India's skill development architecture (aligned with the National Skill Development Mission and Skill India) towards outcome-based, industry-led training rather than input-based government-run centres.

The scheme's performance data—rationalization of targets for 97 Implementing Partners and cancellation for 32 due to poor performance—illustrates the monitoring and accountability mechanisms built into flagship skilling schemes, and is relevant to discussions on effectiveness of public-private partnership models in skill development. The textile sector's labour-intensive nature and its significance for women's employment (highlighted by the high proportion of women beneficiaries in Rajasthan) also ties into broader policy goals of inclusive growth, women's economic empowerment, and social justice provisions for SC/ST communities under India's employment and skilling framework.
